summary.value: The Lamona is an American chicken bred at the USDA research station in Beltsville, Maryland. Starting in 1912, government poultry scientist Harry Lamon blended three breeds: the white Plymouth Rock, the white Leghorn and the silver-gray Dorking. He wanted a hen that laid well and could still go to the table as a reasonably tender bird once her laying days were over, which most laying breeds cannot do. The APA accepted the Lamona in 1933 and the bantam in 1960. It is a mid-sized bird, heavier than a Leghorn but lighter than a Plymouth Rock or Dorking, with white feathers, yellow skin and a single comb. It lays white eggs yet has red earlobes, an unusual mix. Numbers fell sharply by the 1980s, and by 2013 no flock descended from the original birds could be traced, so the breed may be extinct.
